A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CTBench and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and appendices. Original scientific content can be matched across relocation and renumbering. A localized ambiguity in v2 Table 9 limits identification of that experiment's setting.

before.justification: v1 reports original CTBench training and certification results in Table 1, model analyses in Section 5, and additional empirical results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds an implementation/tuning comparison in Appendix A.1 and a comparison of certification outcomes in Table 9.

M1.justification: The training algorithms, CNN7 architecture, losses, batch-normalization fixes, and weight averaging are unchanged. Appendix A.1 explains the existing population-statistics procedure under the name PreciseBN; it does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The established MNIST, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, MNIST-C, and CIFAR-10-C coverage is retained. However, new Table 9 names MNIST while listing radii 2/255 and 8/255, which elsewhere identify CIFAR-10 settings. The PDFs do not resolve whether this adds MNIST test scenarios or contains a mislabeled dataset.

E2.justification: New Table 9 evaluates OVAL alongside MN-BAB in a supplementary comparison of certification outcomes. The original training-method comparisons retain PGD, EDAC, IBP, CROWN-IBP, SABR, TAPS, STAPS, and MTL-IBP.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an IBP comparison using literature hyperparameters, and Table 9 introduces paired-verifier outcome analysis. Existing splits, preprocessing, training schedules, architectures, hyperparameters, and certification timeouts are retained. The first-ten-sample certification note is newly disclosed information, not evidence that an existing protocol changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds an illustrative implementation-versus-tuning check, a qualitative assessment of PreciseBN's limited final-performance effect, and shared-failure analysis across two verifiers. The existing fragmentation, model utilization, propagation tightness, shared-model-mistake, and corruption analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1's checklist explains the absence of repeated experiments and error bars. v2 removes that checklist and newly states that its experiments use the same fixed random seed, contrasting this with literature results selected from three seeds. This is additional seed disclosure, not evidence of increased replication; uncertainty intervals remain absent.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores and plotted results are retained. Table 1 fills PGD/EDAC certification entries with approximately zero, qualified by failure to certify the first ten samples within the timeout. Appendix A.1 adds 93.18% certified accuracy for IBP using literature hyperparameters, alongside the retained tuned 93.80%. New Table 9 reports paired-verifier counts, including 3549/15/6436 for neither/one/both certifying in its first setting.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss expressions, and background reasoning are unchanged. The new discussion about decomposing improvements is qualitative; it adds no formal impossibility result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a unified certified-training benchmark, stronger tuned performance, reduced advantages over improved baselines, and insights into certified models. Minor wording refinements do not alter these claims' scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 qualifies attribution of improvements because batch-normalization fixes enable additional hyperparameter choices. It also explains PreciseBN's small final effect through convergence of batch-normalization statistics. Existing limitations concerning deterministic certification, perturbation norms, and patch robustness are relocated unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit CTBench repository address, clarifies that PreciseBN uses the entire training dataset for test-time statistics, and discloses the ten-sample basis of adversarial-model certification entries. Hardware, hyperparameter tables, and timing information are retained. The checklist's explicit statement about released training and certification logs disappears.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. OVAL and PreciseBN are named using the already cited De Palma et al. (2022) and Wu and Johnson (2021). Alphabetizing and reformatting the bibliography do not add research references.

P1.justification: Most scientific prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. v2 adds a reproducibility statement and discussion subsection, groups retained limitations and broader impacts under Discussion, renumbers the experimental appendices, removes the NeurIPS checklist, and makes limited wording and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: v2 changes title and heading styling, page rules, figure sizing, and float placement. Figure 6 moves to a separate page, Table 1 gains a footnote, Table 2 is reformatted, and a new Table 9 precedes the retained table now numbered 10. Existing plot content is preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency through the repository pointer, seed disclosure, certification-sample qualification, and discussion of attribution limits. The added IBP comparison and verifier analysis provide limited supporting evidence. These gains leave the core benchmark unchanged; Table 9's ambiguous setting and the continued absence of repeated-run uncertainty constrain the improvement.
